pole_convention.note: 2026-08-05 CORRECTION, supersedes the 2026-08-04 rule below. The 2026-08-04 rule 'the housing_3_vertical asset's BULB FACE points along its own LOCAL +Y' is WRONG, and it aimed the smooth BACK of every head at its approach for a whole day. What that measurement actually found was the LENS PLANE (local y=0), not the face. Full housing-local anatomy, measured on sig_NE: hood_square visor y[-0.302,-0.106]; base bezel/socket body y[-0.112,+0.059]; the flat yellow face panel (border + surround, 4 mm thick, carrying 'trafficLight__front' and '__back' GeomSubsets) y[-0.084,-0.080]; bulb lens discs ('on' and 'off', coplanar) y=0.000. The visor protrudes toward -Y and the face panel's front subset looks the same way, so the composite's TRUE FRONT IS LOCAL -Y, and the lenses shipped 0.082 m BEHIND the opaque face panel -- which is why the hoods read as empty dark sockets while the lens edges glowed out the back of the head (the user's exact complaint). CORRECTED RULE, unchanged at the survey level: yaw_deg is still the assembly ROOT's rotateZ, still equals face_deg - 90, and face_deg is still (approach heading at the stop line) + 180. What changed is entirely LOCAL to the housing child and lives in build_intersection_dressing.py: HOUSING_LOCAL_YAW=180 spins the composite about its own axis so local -Y (the hooded front) lands on face_deg, and BULB_LOCAL_Y=-0.118 seats the lenses 6 mm proud of the bezel lip (-0.105 was tried and REJECTED: the bezel aperture necks to r=0.120 at y=-0.1094 vs the 0.1205 lens, leaving only a crescent visible; caught as a doc/live mismatch by the 2026-08-05 Codex audit). Because both are local to the housing, the survey yaws, ARM_LOCAL_OFFSET and add_signal_masts.py's arm aiming (which reads only the housing's TRANSLATE op) are all untouched -- that coupling did NOT have to be re-derived.
pole_convention.note_2026_08_04_superseded: 2026-08-04 REWORK. yaw_deg is the assembly ROOT's xformOp:rotateZ (build_intersection_dressing.place_and_reference). The housing_3_vertical asset's BULB FACE points along its own LOCAL +Y (measured live: with root yaw 0 the bulb discs are 0.04 m thin in Y, 0.24 m wide in X, and sit at the +Y extreme of the housing box), so world face azimuth = yaw_deg + 90. The old yaws assumed the face was local +X, which is why every head read side-on to its approach. RULE: yaw_deg = face_deg - 90, where face_deg = (approach heading at the stop line) + 180, i.e. the head looks straight back down its approach corridor. The 0.5 m housing offset (ARM_LOCAL_OFFSET, along root-local +X) then automatically points roadway-ward for all four poles.
pole_convention.pole_mounted_props: 2026-08-05. Everything that belongs to a signal pole is now authored UNDER its assembly root, in the pole's local frame, so it cannot drift away from the pole: mast + arm + xwbutton (add_signal_masts.py) and housing + ped_housing/box + ped panels (build_intersection_dressing.py). Mount math for anything hung off the mast: the mast axis is the assembly root's local origin, radius MAST_RADIUS=0.06. A prop whose asset places its body at local y>=b with its own +Y as the outward face mounts at pole-local (r*cos(t), r*sin(t)) with t = face_deg - yaw_deg and r = MAST_RADIUS - b, and its own rotateZ = face_deg - yaw_deg - 90. Measured b: crosswalk_signal_01_inst = 0.045 (r=+0.015), crosswalk_button_01_inst = 0.129 (r=-0.069; that asset budgets for a 0.129 m-radius pole, so its origin sits slightly BEHIND our thinner mast's axis).
pole_convention.placement: 2026-08-04 (2nd pass) NEAR-SIDE-RIGHT. Superseded the far-side-right mapping authored earlier the same day (user: 'The traffic light poles need to be on the incoming traffic side. Currently, they are exactly on the opposite side.'). Each pole now stands on the corner sidewalk pad that its own approach's traffic reaches FIRST, on the driver's right at the stop line, bulb face aimed back down that approach. Measured curb pads (unchanged, from the city street mesh): SW x[-35.6,-30.7] y[69.4,73.9], SE x[-16.4,-11.4] y[68.1,72.5], NW x[-35.5,-30.3] y[84.7,89.2], NE x[-15.9,-11.0] y[83.3,87.6]. NEW mapping (diagonal swap of the far-side one): NB->SE pad, SB->NW pad, EB->SW pad, WB->NE pad. yaw_deg depends only on the approach (yaw = approach_heading + 90), so the yaws swapped diagonally with the 'controls'/'faces_approach' groups; the 0.5 m ARM_LOCAL_OFFSET along root-local +X still lands roadway-ward on all four (SE head goes W, NW head goes E, SW head goes N, NE head goes S). Positions are constrained by (a) staying on the pad with >=0.3 m edge margin, (b) staying >=0.3 m outside every crosswalk polygon, (c) camera clearance: each head's projected footprint must not overlap the intersection-box ROI in any of the 4 RTSP streams (1920x1080, hfov 70 -> half-widths tan35=0.7002 horizontal / 0.3939 vertical; head measured live as 0.48x0.36x1.056 m, so +-0.30 m horizontal / +-0.53 m vertical). Measured result (u,v normalized to the half-frame; |u|>1 or |v|>1 = out of frame): sig_SE head is OUT of cam_SE (u=+1.20 at 2.5 m) and cam_SW, and only appears small and high in cam_NW (u=+0.08, v=+0.61, 28.9 m) and cam_NE (u=-0.81, 19.7 m). sig_SW head is OUT of cam_SE/cam_SW/cam_NW, small in cam_NE (23.4 m). sig_NE head is OUT of cam_NE (u=-1.49 at 6.4 m) and cam_SE, small in cam_SW/cam_NW. COMPROMISE, sig_NW: no point on the NW pad puts the assembly out of cam_NW's frame (cam_NW eye (-35.5,91,5.2) sits directly over the pad's NW corner and looks SE across it). Also learned the hard way here: the head-only occlusion model is NOT sufficient - the MAST (0.12 m cylinder, ground to 5.35 m) must be projected as a column too. The first pick (-30.6,85.3) passed the head test (u=+0.03 but v=+0.61+-0.18, above the ROI) and then the live RTSP frame showed its mast running down the exact vertical centreline of cam_NW at 7.6 m. Final pick (-33.1,84.9) is at the west end of the pad's BUILDABLE part - note x[-35.5,-33.4] of that pad is the XW_W crosswalk, so -33.1 (0.3 m clear of the stripes) is the furthest-from-axis position available. Whole assembly projects at cam_NW u=+0.51 (head, +-0.07) to +0.64 (mast top), a quarter frame right of centre, at 6.2 m; out of frame in cam_NE, small and high in cam_SE (23.7 m) / cam_SW (16.0 m). Cost: SB driver bearing 38.1 deg right at 12.4 m instead of 28.5 deg at 10.4 m. ped_housing MOVED from {sig_SE, sig_NW} to {sig_SE, sig_SW} (build_intersection_dressing.PED_SIGNAL_IDS): light_controller derives ped_group from the pole's vehicle group, so sig_SE (now NS_through) -> ped_cross_NS and sig_SW (now EW_through) -> ped_cross_EW, one housing per ped group instead of two on the same group. Both land on real crosswalk landings: sig_SE (-15.3,68.7) is 1.6 m east of XW_S's east edge (x=-16.9) with y inside XW_S's band [64.8,68.8] -> the XW_S east landing, correct for ped_cross_NS; sig_SW (-35.0,73.6) is 0.3 m south of XW_W's south edge (y=73.9) with x inside XW_W's band [-37.4,-33.4] -> the XW_W south landing, correct for ped_cross_EW. sig_NW is the only pole not on a crosswalk landing, which is why it carries no ped housing. Free-air verified live (TraverseInstanceProxies world-bbox scan, 12104 meshes, 1.2 m radius, z 0..5.8): sig_SE / sig_NW / sig_NE have ZERO non-signal meshes above z=0.3 within 1.2 m; sig_SW's nearest is the SW block building (x<=-35.64, y<=72.46) at 1.19 m Euclidean from the mast, and its head offsets north, away from it. All four sit on Street_Modern_Standard_Pavement at z=0 (sidewalk), same surface class as the previous poles.

NB heading at stop line (-22.02,62.74) is 86.09 deg -> face 266.09 (south-southwest) -> yaw 176.09. World face azimuth (math convention, 0=+X/east, 90=+Y/north) = pole_yaw_deg + ped_yaw_deg + 90. Solving for target azimuth 180 (west): ped_yaw_deg = 180 - 176.09 - 90 = -86.09. west_arm_lane_model.measured: 2026-08-05. THE WEST ARM IS DIAGONAL -- every axis-aligned y constant previously used here was wrong. The double yellow is /World/CityCm/.../Shape_88/Street_Modern_Standard_CenterLineMarkings_13/mesh, a single 4-point textured quad whose 0.49 m wide strip runs from (-135.27,84.479) to (-37.36,77.771); its y[77.52,84.72] AABB is the sweep of that DIAGONAL, not three parallel lines (an earlier reading of this same AABB as 'centre 81.12 = centreline, edges = lane lines, 3.6 m lanes' was a coincidence of arithmetic and is superseded). The survey meta note 'E-W street centreline y drops ~0.064 per +x metre' applies here too, not only east of the box. Road edges from the curb meshes Shape_89/Street_Modern_Standard_Curbs_64 (south) and Shape_90/Street_Modern_Standard_Curbs_65 (north), same -0.0705 slope.
west_arm_lane_model.note: The west arm is a THREE-lane road: ONE eastbound lane south of the double yellow (3.66 m, centre offset -1.83) and TWO westbound lanes north of it (7.07 m). The dashed white line visible in plan view is the WB lane divider, north of the centreline -- there is no dashed line on the EB side, because there is only one EB lane. This agrees with lane EB_1's own closure_note ('single EB lane') and with WB_1's polyline y=82.85, which is 3.39 m north of the centreline at x=-62, i.e. the inner WB lane. Consequence for the closure: closing EB_1 closes the ENTIRE eastbound direction, so the taper runs from the double yellow down to the south curb rather than between two same-direction lanes. Also noted: EB_1's polyline is authored as a STRAIGHT line at y=79.35 while the real lane centre is y_c(x)-1.83 (77.63 at x=-62), so it is up to ~1.7 m off and at the east end sits north of the centreline. Harmless while EB is closed and unspawned; re-opening EB traffic needs that polyline re-cut along y_c(x)-1.83 -- a scenario decision for the user, not for the dressing scripts.
west_arm_lane_model.see_also: 2026-08-05: geometry.curbs.promoted_west_arm_prose carries the re-measured version of these keys.  The centreline here is exact; the curb dydx -0.0705 is a bbox artifact (true -0.068530) and the cross-section half-widths are 0.15 m off.  Prefer geometry.curbs.lines.* for anything geometric.

closure.spec: 2026-08-10 rebuild for the WB outer-lane closure, regularised from the user's live GUI arrangement (captured 2026-08-10). Offsets are from the DIAGONAL centreline y_c(x); positive = NORTH = the westbound side. WB traffic travels EAST -> WEST (decreasing x), so drivers meet the legs in the order listed: advance-warning barricade, arrow board at the taper head, MERGING taper (curb -> work offset, closing the outer lane), tangent delineation alongside the work area, TERMINATION taper back out to the curb. Every cone is generated from these legs by build_intersection_dressing.closure_cone_positions(), so the layout stays tied to the measured lane geometry.
closure.cone_offset_note: work 3.90 is 0.39 m north of the WB lane divider (3.5082); with the 0.19 m base radius of TrafficCone_A07_71cm the cone's south edge sits at 3.71, 0.20 m clear of the divider. curb 6.62 leaves 0.40 m to the north curb (7.0164), i.e. 0.21 m of cone-edge clearance.

taper.spec: 2026-08-05 rebuild. All offsets are measured from the DIAGONAL centreline y_c(x) in west_arm_lane_model (negative = south = the EB side). The cone line starts UPSTREAM (west) just inside the double yellow and slants to just inside the south curb DOWNSTREAM (east), closing the single EB lane. From the EB driver's seat (looking east: left=north, right=south, near low in frame) that is a '/' running bottom-left to top-right, the orientation the user asked for. CAPTURE NOTE: in a north-up/east-right TOP-DOWN view the SAME line necessarily appears as a backslash; take plan views with up=(1,0,0) (east up, the driver's heading up) to see the '/'. EVERY cone is south of the centreline by construction, which is the actual bug being fixed: the previous hardcoded line ran y 77.6 -> 80.6 while y_c runs 79.46 -> 78.02 over the same span, so its upstream half sat NORTH of the double yellow in the oncoming WB lanes and read as diverting EB traffic into oncoming.

tangent.note: downstream tangent: cones held just inside the south curb so the closed lane stays delineated alongside the work area.

work_area.note: Everything lives in the closed EB lane, downstream (east) of the taper, at y_c(x) + offset. Arrow board at the upstream (west) head, facing west, arrow pointing right/south.

turns.note: Random left/right turns at intersection A. `enabled:false` means TrafficSim builds no route objects at all, so live behaviour is byte-identical to the through-only pilot; the offline checker and the test suite force-build instead. Exit targets are the P1-MEASURED lane-centre fits in geometry.curbs.derived_lane_centers, never the authored lane polylines (those carry up to 0.36 m of sign-reversing chord error). The fillet's INCOMING tangent is the authored approach polyline segment, so the join to the lane the vehicle is actually driving stays C1; the fillet absorbs the authored-vs-measured offset.
turns.vlim_decel_note: Rate at which the P4 backward pass propagates the arc's speed limit upstream. Lowered from B_COMF=3.0 on measurement: vlim caps IDM's DESIRED speed, and IDM only brakes at 3 m/s^2 once it is ~22 percent over that cap, so a 3.0 profile was tracked with a standing error and produced 3.50 m/s^2 of realised lateral acceleration against the 2.0 target. 1.5 gives 2.69 m/s^2 and starts braking 48 m before the fillet instead of 23 m. Full table in vehicle_lib VLIM_DECEL_DEFAULT.
turns.class_permissions_note: movement codes a class may take. A class absent from this map may take any movement. Buses and bicycles are through-only (locked decision); P3 still consumes exactly one movement draw per arrival and discards it for them, so the arrival stream is unperturbed.
turns.radius_selection: chosen with scripts/turns/build_check_routes.py -- see that script's report for the per-route swept-path margins on BOTH sides (inner corner return vs outer/far curb).

NB_1:L.note: 2026-08-10: exit_lane null -> 'WB_1'. Its 45 m tail runs on the ew_west_WB_1 fit and the re-cut WB_1 IS that fit from x=-34 west, so the two are collinear -- without a declared merge build_conflict_points raises on the sub-20-deg crossing (measured min separation 0.109 m). The WB_1 re-cut was aimed to put B (-30.221, 79.034) inside MERGE_MAX_OFFSET_M of the WB_1 polyline (measured 0.588 m) precisely so this merge CAN be declared. The old P2 'head-on hazard vs EB_1' is RESOLVED: the re-cut EB_1 is 3.51 m south of this tail (the 0.218 m figure was measured against the wrong old EB_1 line).

SB_1:L.note: 2026-08-10: exit_lane null -> 'EB_1'. EB_1 is a live lane again and its re-cut east-arm segment IS the ew_east_EB_1 fit this route is tangent to, so the standing P2 hazard (tail 0.266 m from EB_1, same direction, no merge bookkeeping) is now expressed as a declared merge instead of an accepted overlap.

EB_1:R.note: 2026-08-10: right turn onto the RIGHTMOST southbound lane (SB_2, offset -5.26), mirroring NB_1:R -> ew_east_EB_2. SB_2 carries no lane object, so no merge.

EB_1:L.note: 2026-08-10: left turn onto the INNERMOST northbound lane, mirroring SB_1:L -> ew_east_EB_1. NB_1's north-arm polyline sits within MERGE_MAX_OFFSET_M of that fit, so the merge is declared.

SB_1:R.reason: WORK-ZONE TURN RESTRICTION, forced by geometry and caught by vehicle_lib's own conflict-point audit. A southbound right turn's natural destination is the west arm's OUTER westbound lane (ew_west_WB_2) -- that lane IS the closure, and this route's 45 m tail ran straight down the middle of it (offset +5.26) through the whole cone band. The only open westbound lane is the INNER one, which is already the destination of NB_1:L; routing both onto ew_west_WB_1 makes the two fillets join the same line tangentially (measured min path separation 0.003 m) and build_conflict_points raises TurnBuildError: a sub-20-deg crossing between live geoms closer than CP_SHALLOW_MIN_SEP_M=2.0 m that cannot be expressed as a declared merge (the merge is validated at the tangent point B, and no radius that keeps the swept path on the road puts B within MERGE_MAX_OFFSET_M=1.0 m of either the re-cut WB_1 polyline or the other route). The movement whose own lane is closed is the one that gets prohibited; NB_1:L keeps the open inner lane. SB_1 mix 0.70/0.15/0.15 -> 0.85 T / 0.15 L. REVERT with the closure: restore this entry to turns.movements and put SB_1 back on 0.70/0.15/0.15.
